summary: isCancel's type guard narrows to CanceledError<T> instead of the old Cancel type (type-level return-type change; the CommonJS typings followed in 1.17.0)
The default params serializer now percent-encodes '[' and ']' (%5B/%5D) in query values instead of leaving them literal
Under Bun the package exports now resolve to the Node.js build (http adapter) instead of the browser build (xhr/fetch adapters)

Config merging and the adapters read only own properties of config objects (and from 1.15.2 produce null-prototype configs), so values inherited through a config's prototype chain are ignored where they used to be honored; tightened further in 1.15.2, 1.17.0, 1.18.0 and 1.20.0
The fetch adapter now enforces maxBodyLength and maxContentLength, which it silently ignored before 1.16.0
The fetch adapter now sends a default User-Agent: axios/<version> header where the runtime allows it, matching the http adapter, where it sent none before
Protocol detection (parseProtocol) now requires a colon after the scheme, so loosely formed protocol strings that used to match no longer do
Requests sent through a proxy keep a user-supplied Host header instead of having it overwritten by the proxy path
Basic-auth credentials embedded in the request URL are percent-decoded before use (https://user:p%40ss@host sends p@ss) instead of being sent as written
Non-ASCII strings are encoded with a spec-correct UTF-8 encoder instead of the deprecated unescape(), so output bytes can differ for non-ASCII input
FormData serialisation and formDataToJSON now stop at a default nesting depth of 100 and throw ERR_FORM_DATA_DEPTH_EXCEEDED beyond it, where nesting was unbounded before
http:/https: URLs missing the // (https:example.com, http:/example.com) now reject with AxiosError ERR_INVALID_URL instead of being silently normalised and sent
NO_PROXY matching now treats 0.0.0.0 and IPv6 :: (and their compressed forms) as local addresses that bypass the proxy, where they previously did not match
The Node http adapter strips caller-specified sensitive headers (Authorization, API-key style headers) when a redirect goes to another origin instead of forwarding them
data: URIs whose media type contains extra slash separators now reject with ERR_INVALID_URL instead of being parsed
With the fetch adapter maxRedirects: 0 now prevents redirects from being followed (manual redirect mode, exposing the 3xx or an opaque redirect) instead of being ignored
NO_PROXY entries now accept IPv4 and IPv6 CIDR ranges, so 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 bypass the proxy for every destination where such entries previously matched nothing
HttpStatusCode.PayloadTooLarge (413) is deprecated in favor of the new HttpStatusCode.ContentTooLarge
HttpStatusCode.UnprocessableEntity (422) is deprecated in favor of the new HttpStatusCode.UnprocessableContent

config()'s runtime log lines drop the [dotenv@x.y.z] prefix: the injection message becomes '◇ injecting env (n) from .env // tip: …', debug lines '┆ …' and warnings '⚠ …', where before they read '[dotenv@17.x.x] injecting env (n) from .env -- tip: …', '[dotenv@17.x.x][DEBUG] …' and '[dotenv@17.x.x][WARN] …'

populate()'s options parameter is typed DotenvPopulateOptions (debug and override only) instead of DotenvConfigOptions, so passing config-only keys such as path, quiet or encoding to populate() is now a TypeScript error (runtime unchanged; not in the changelog, seen in lib/main.d.ts)
The injection message wording changes from 'injecting env (n) from .env' to 'injected env (n) from .env'

Options passed to config() now take precedence over DOTENV_* and DOTENV_CONFIG_* environment variables, where 17.2.0 documented the opposite (a DOTENV_CONFIG_* variable overrode code-set options such as {quiet: false})

DOTENV_CONFIG_PATH, DOTENV_CONFIG_ENCODING and DOTENV_CONFIG_OVERRIDE (and the new DOTENV_PATH/ENCODING/OVERRIDE/FAST names) now set defaults for every config() call, where before a direct config() call honoured only DOTENV_CONFIG_DEBUG and DOTENV_CONFIG_QUIET and the rest applied only through the dotenv/config preload

.env.vault support is removed: config() no longer decrypts a .env.vault file when DOTENV_KEY is set (the DOTENV_KEY option, the DOTENV_KEY and DOTENV_CONFIG_DOTENV_KEY env vars and the DotenvConfigOptions.DOTENV_KEY type are gone; it always reads the plain .env), and the decrypt() export (plus _configVault/_parseVault) no longer exists
config()'s '◇ injected env (n) from .env' message is written to stderr (console.error) instead of stdout (console.log); debug lines stay on stdout
The random '// tip: …' suffix (dotenvx/vestauth promotions and option hints, present since 17.1.0) is dropped from the injection message, which now ends after the file list

Preload configuration is removed in favour of the new dotenv run CLI: node -r dotenv/config no longer reads dotenv_config_<option>=value command-line arguments, and the dotenv/lib/env-options and dotenv/lib/cli-options subpath exports are gone; import 'dotenv/config' itself still works (but logged by default until 18.0.4, where 17.x preloads were quiet)

import 'dotenv/config' (and node -r dotenv/config) defaults quiet to true again, so it prints no injection message unless DOTENV_QUIET=false or DOTENV_CONFIG_QUIET=false is set; 18.0.0 to 18.0.3 logged by default

populate()'s return type DotenvPopulateOutput declares its values as string | undefined instead of string, so under strict null checks a populated value must be narrowed before use as a string (a declaration correction; runtime unchanged)

With the 'extended' query parser req.query became a prototype-less plain object (no inherited Object.prototype properties) instead of a normal object; REVERTED in 5.2.1 (CVE-2024-51999 was rejected), so the pinned version has the old behavior
res.redirect now emits a deprecation warning when called with no URL, a non-string URL, or a non-number status, where before such calls were accepted silently
express.json/urlencoded/raw/text (body-parser 2.3) throw at parser construction when the limit option is invalid instead of silently disabling the body size limit
res.attachment(), res.download() and res.sendFile() now emit Content-Disposition filenames that are valid HTTP tokens without quotes (filename=user.html) where they were always quoted before
The default error handler logs the whole error object (including cause and library-specific properties) instead of only err.stack
req.fresh (and so res.send's 304 handling) now evaluates conditional-request validators for QUERY requests as well as GET/HEAD; a QUERY with a matching ETag previously always got the full response
The HTML body sent by res.redirect() when HTML is accepted now has , and <body> wrappers instead of a bare <p> fragment
app.render(view, null, callback) is now treated like omitted or empty options instead of throwing on the null locals
res.send() keeps the existing parameters of a Content-Type when it appends charset (text/plain; foo=bar -> text/plain; foo=bar; charset=utf-8) instead of dropping them
res.send() no longer throws when the response's Content-Type header fails to parse; it leaves the header as set

Importing a CommonJS module from ESM now exposes a broader set of named exports and one shared module instance across importers; the __esModule/Babel default unwrapping 30.4.0 added was reverted in 30.4.1, so the default export is always module.exports as in Node

A .js file containing ESM syntax but no "type":"module" marker is now loaded as native ESM (also for require() on Node 24.9+) instead of failing to parse as CommonJS; 30.5.0 narrowed this so such files inside a "type":"commonjs" package or with a .cjs extension throw the CJS parse error as Node does

ESM import attributes are now validated (an unsupported attribute, or a type that does not match the module, throws) and importing JSON without `with { type: 'json' }` prints a deprecation warning that will become an error in Jest 31; before, attributes were ignored and JSON imported silently (30.5.0 emits the warning once per test file)

On Node 24.9+, resolution and import-attribute errors anywhere in an ESM graph are raised before any of its CommonJS dependencies execute (Node's run-nothing-on-a-broken-graph order); older Node keeps the previous linking-time execution order

Calling module.register() or module.registerHooks() inside a test now throws an actionable error; before, the hooks silently attached to the loader running Jest itself and stayed registered for later test files in the worker

The default resolver now honors the module-sync export condition, so a package exposing an ESM entry point for require() resolves to the file Node would pick instead of failing with Cannot find module
When Node runs with --preserve-symlinks or NODE_PRESERVE_SYMLINKS=1 the default resolver no longer realpaths symlinked modules, matching Node; before it always resolved symlinks to their targets
process.getBuiltinModule() inside a test now returns the sandbox's process and the hooked node:module rather than the host runtime's
@jest/source-map's exported getCallsite() is deprecated in favor of SourceMapSupport#getCallsite
@jest/environment-jsdom-abstract (and so jest-environment-jsdom) now declares @types/jsdom as a peer dependency the project must satisfy instead of bundling it as a dependency

reporters, coverageReporters, workerIdleMemoryLimit, cwd and runnerOptions are removed from the project config types and, like maxWorkers and coverageThreshold, now trigger a validation warning when set in a project config instead of being silently ignored
The RailSymbol icon export is marked @deprecated (a brand icon slated for removal in v1), where before it carried no deprecation tag
The chrome icon is renamed chromium: Chromium is the canonical export and Chrome remains only as an alias of it (both tagged @deprecated as brand icons)

The fingerprint icon is renamed fingerprint-pattern and the notes mark the import change breaking: FingerprintPattern is the new export, the Fingerprint named export survives only as an alias, and the per-icon module dist/esm/icons/fingerprint.js is no longer published (the dynamic-icon name 'fingerprint' still resolves)

flip-horizontal and flip-vertical are renamed square-centerline-dashed-horizontal and square-centerline-dashed-vertical; FlipHorizontal and FlipVertical remain as aliases of the new SquareCenterlineDashedHorizontal/Vertical exports

All brand icons are removed: the exports Chrome, Chromium, Codepen, Codesandbox, Dribbble, Facebook, Figma, Framer, Github, Gitlab, Instagram, Linkedin, Pocket, RailSymbol, Slack, Trello, Twitch, Twitter and Youtube (with their *Icon/Lucide* variants, icon modules and dynamic-icon names) no longer exist, where 0.x still shipped them as deprecated exports
The UMD bundle is dropped: dist/umd/lucide-react.js and lucide-react.min.js (the main:umd and unpkg entries) are no longer published, leaving only the ESM and CJS builds
The podcast icon is replaced by the new mic-signal and mic-audio-lines icons: Podcast remains only as an alias of MicSignal and now renders the mic-signal artwork instead of the old podcast design

The emoticon icons are redrawn and renamed after their Unicode emoji: angry→face-angry, annoyed→face-expressionless, laugh→face-grinning, meh→face-neutral, frown→face-slightly-frowning, smile→face-slightly-smiling; Angry, Annoyed, Laugh, Meh, Frown and Smile remain as aliases of the new exports

The trash icon's own design is removed in favour of trash-2: the Trash export now renders the former trash-2 artwork and Trash2 remains only as an alias of Trash (its metadata marks the alias deprecated), where before they were two different icons

The absoluteStrokeWidth prop (on icon components and LucideProvider) is marked @deprecated in favour of the new nonScalingStroke prop, which sets vector-effect=non-scaling-stroke on the paths instead of rescaling stroke-width

Per-icon ESM modules (lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/<name>.mjs; the CJS build is a single bundle) export __iconData, an object {name, size, node}, instead of the bare __iconNode node array; __iconNode is only declared (as deprecated) in the types and is no longer exported at runtime, and DynamicIconModule now reads __iconData
The exported IconNode type is marked @deprecated in favour of LucideIconNode[] (and the new LucideIconData object type); IconNode's element names widen from an SVG tag-name union to string
SwissFranc, BadgeSwissFranc and ReceiptSwissFranc are marked @deprecated (the depicted symbol is obsolete), where before they carried no deprecation tag

flip-horizontal-2 and flip-vertical-2 are renamed triangles-centerline-dashed-horizontal and triangles-centerline-dashed-vertical; FlipHorizontal2 and FlipVertical2 remain as aliases of the new TrianglesCenterlineDashedHorizontal/Vertical exports
The text-select icon is renamed square-dashed-text: SquareDashedText is the canonical export and TextSelect (like the older TextSelection) remains only as an alias of it

The ESM build switches from .js to .mjs files: the module entry is dist/esm/lucide-react.mjs and per-icon modules are dist/esm/icons/<name>.mjs, so deep imports of the former dist/esm/*.js paths no longer resolve (CJS paths are unchanged)
The Document class's _id type parameter defaults to ObjectId instead of unknown, so _id on an un-parameterized Document is typed as ObjectId.
The browser build is removed from the mongoose package; use the separate @mongoosejs/browser package instead.
bson is no longer a direct dependency of mongoose; BSON types come from mongodb/lib/bson, so code that resolved the bson package through mongoose's dependency tree may no longer find it.
SchemaType caster, casterConstructor and $embeddedSchemaType are removed; use embeddedSchemaType (the element schema type) and Constructor (the subdocument constructor).
create() and insertOne() no longer take a generic parameter; the argument must match Partial of the raw doc type (with query-style casting), where 8.x let any value through.
pre/post hooks on custom methods and statics only run when the method is async or returns a promise; callback-style custom methods are no longer hooked.
The Document class no longer declares an id: any property; id is a string virtual appended to TVirtuals on hydrated documents.
Document.prototype.updateOne() no longer accepts a callback as its third argument; it only returns a query.
SchemaType/Schema doValidate() returns a promise that rejects on a validation error instead of taking a callback, and update validators and save hooks run asynchronously as part of the same change.
Queries no longer record the stack trace of their first execution (_executionStack) and the skipOriginalStackTraces option that disabled it is removed.
The FilterQuery TypeScript type is renamed to QueryFilter and FilterQuery is no longer exported.
find(null), findOne(null) and similar calls throw an error instead of ignoring the filter and returning documents.
Mongoose no longer sets background: true on indexes by default and Schema.prototype.index() no longer accepts the background option.
InferRawDocType adds _id: ObjectId to the inferred type, where 8.x inferred only the declared schema fields; InferRawDocTypeWithout_id (added in 9.0.2) restores the old shape.
isAsync middleware (pre('save', true, function(next, done))) is no longer supported; use async functions or return a promise.
isValidObjectId() returns false for numbers and new Types.ObjectId(number) throws, where 8.x returned true and built an ObjectId from the number.
The bundled MongoDB Node.js driver moves from 6.x to 7.x, bringing that driver's own breaking changes.
The minimum supported Node.js version is 20.19.0; older Node versions that 8.x supported are dropped.
The noListener option is removed from connections and useDb(); passing it throws, and useDb() accepts only { useCache }.
Pluralization rules are corrected and extended (for example model Virus now maps to collection viruses), changing the default collection name for affected model names.
Pre middleware no longer receives a next() callback; hooks must be async functions or return a promise, where 8.x accepted callback-style pre hooks.
The promiseOrCallback helper export is removed; require('mongoose').promiseOrCallback is undefined.
RootQuerySelector, Condition and related filter types are consolidated with the MongoDB driver's filter types instead of Mongoose's own definitions.
QueryFilter (the first argument of find()/findOne() etc.) types top-level keys from the schema, so wrong value types and unknown operators are TypeScript errors instead of resolving to any.
The third argument to Model()/Document() must be an options object; passing a boolean skipId is no longer supported.
Calling deleteOne() on a subdocument no longer fires its deleteOne hooks immediately; they run only when the parent is saved or deleted so the subdocument is actually removed.
In TypeScript, this inside default() and required() functions is HydratedDocument and inside validate() is HydratedDocument | Query, replacing the looser previous this type.
Passing an aggregation-pipeline array to updateOne()/updateMany()/findOneAndUpdate() throws unless updatePipeline: true is set per query or via mongoose.set(); 8.x sent the pipeline through uncast.
Query.use$geoWithin is removed and $geoWithin is never rewritten to $within.
UUID schema paths hold bson.UUID instances (serialized as hex strings in JSON) instead of Mongoose Buffers that a getter converted to strings.
A virtual populate ref function declared on a subdocument schema is called with that subdocument instead of the top-level document.
The 'Duplicate schema index' warning is emitted when indexes are built (createIndexes/syncIndexes/autoIndex) and names the model, instead of when the schema is compiled.
The exported TypeScript types for the long-removed Model.mapReduce() and geoSearch() are removed.
The new and returnOriginal options of findOneAndUpdate()/findOneAndReplace() are deprecated and print a runtime warning; use returnDocument: 'after' | 'before' (also settable globally).
Document.prototype.getChanges() is deprecated in favor of the new $getChanges() alias.

The email provider's default identifier normalizer now throws 'Invalid email address format.' for an address containing a double quote, not exactly one '@', an empty local or domain part, or a domain without a dot; before it only lower-cased, trimmed and split on '@'
GET /api/auth/session and /api/auth/csrf responses now carry Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store with Pragma: no-cache and Expires: 0; before they sent only Content-Type
The optional nodemailer peer dependency range moves from ^6.6.5 to ^7.0.7, so the email provider now expects nodemailer 7 instead of 6
The optional @auth/core peer dependency pin moves from 0.34.2 to 0.34.3
The GitHub provider now sets issuer to https://github.com/login/oauth by default (it was unset), so openid-client's unconditional iss check on the callback passes without configuring it

The email provider's default identifier normalizer applies Unicode NFKC normalization before validating the address, so homoglyphs of '@' are collapsed and rejected; before validation ran on the raw string
getToken() returns null when the Authorization header's Bearer value is malformed percent-encoding instead of throwing from decodeURIComponent
An explicitly configured NEXTAUTH_URL now takes precedence over the auto-detected forwarded host when VERCEL or AUTH_TRUST_HOST is set; before the forwarded host won in trusted-host mode

OAuth state, nonce and PKCE check cookies now record the provider that minted them and the callback throws when a different provider handles it; before any provider's callback accepted them (sign-ins in flight across the upgrade fail once)
Built-in AMP support (`useAmp` from `next/amp`, page `config.amp`, the `amp` next.config key) is deprecated with a warning ahead of removal in 16.
Config keys renamed with auto-migration of the old name: `experimental.typedRoutes` becomes top-level `typedRoutes` (now stable), and `experimental.dynamicIO` becomes `experimental.cacheComponents`.
`next/image` now warns when a local `src` carries a query string while `images.localPatterns` is unset, because 16 will require a matching localPatterns entry.
`next/image` now warns when a `quality` other than 75 is used while `images.qualities` is unset, because 16 will restrict qualities to the configured list.
The `legacyBehavior` prop of `next/link` (child `<a>` wrapper mode) is deprecated with a warning; use `<Link>` without a child anchor instead.
The `next lint` command is deprecated (warns, removed in 16); projects should run ESLint or Biome directly instead of `next lint`.
The exported `NextRequest` type no longer exposes Next.js-internal members; code that typed against those internals no longer compiles.
`unstable_rootParams` (from `next/server`) is deprecated with a warning; the replacement is the `next/root-params` module.
On the 15.5 line, Next.js now refuses to run with TypeScript >= 7.0 and exits with an error (the 16.x line gained TypeScript 7 support instead).
`serverRuntimeConfig` / `publicRuntimeConfig` in next.config (read via `getConfig()` from `next/config`) now log a deprecation warning; environment variables are the replacement.
Built-in AMP support is removed: `useAmp`/`next/amp`, page `config.amp` and the `amp` next.config key no longer exist.
`next build` output no longer prints the `Size` and `First Load JS` columns per route (and the manifests behind them are gone).

The new router/prefetch implementation (`experimental.clientSegmentCache`) is on by default: prefetches are per segment with layout deduplication and incremental fetching, so navigations issue more, smaller requests.
Config keys moved out of `experimental` to the top level (old location deprecated): `reactCompiler`, `cacheComponents`, `cacheLife` profiles and `cacheHandlers`.
`next dev` loads next.config only in the server process, so `process.argv` inside the config no longer contains `'dev'`; use `NODE_ENV` or the config `phase` instead.
The default browserslist targets moved to Baseline widely-available browsers (Chrome/Edge/Firefox 111+, Safari 16.4+), changing the JS/CSS output for projects without their own browserslist.
`next dev` now writes to `.next/dev` (including generated types) instead of sharing `.next` with `next build`, so dev and build can run concurrently.
The `devIndicators` options `appIsrStatus`, `buildActivity` and `buildActivityPosition` are removed (the indicator itself remains).
`next dev` and `next build` now acquire a lockfile on the dist directory, so a second `next dev` or `next build` on the same project fails instead of running.
`@next/eslint-plugin-next` and `eslint-config-next` now default to ESLint flat config; the legacy `.eslintrc` `extends: 'next'` form is no longer supported at v16.
The `experimental.dynamicIO` and `experimental.useCache` flags are removed; the behavior is enabled with top-level `cacheComponents: true`.

Partial Prerendering config is removed: `experimental.ppr` (including `'incremental'`) and the route-level `export const experimental_ppr` are no longer accepted; PPR is opted into via `cacheComponents`.
The deprecated `experimental.turbo` config object is removed; Turbopack options must live under the top-level `turbopack` key.
`images.imageSizes` default no longer includes 16, so `next/image` srcsets stop offering a 16px candidate unless configured.
The image optimizer now refuses to fetch from local/private IP addresses by default; `images.dangerouslyAllowLocalIP: true` restores the old behavior.
A local `next/image` `src` with a query string now needs a matching `images.localPatterns` entry (with `search`); previously any query string was optimized.
`images.maximumRedirects` default changed from unlimited to 3 redirects when fetching remote images.
`images.minimumCacheTTL` default changed from 60 seconds to 14400 seconds (4 hours) for optimized images without cache-control headers.
`images.qualities` default changed from allowing 1-100 to `[75]`; a `quality` prop is coerced to the closest configured value and other `q` values on `/_next/image` return 400.
The `images.domains` config is deprecated with a warning; use `images.remotePatterns`.

Metadata route functions receive Promises instead of plain values: image generators (`opengraph-image`, `twitter-image`, `icon`, `apple-icon`) get `params` and `id` as Promises, and `sitemap` gets `id` as a Promise.
The `middleware` file convention and `middleware` export are deprecated in favor of `proxy.ts` exporting `proxy`, which runs only on the Node.js runtime (keep `middleware` for the Edge runtime).

middleware-named APIs renamed to proxy (old names kept as deprecated aliases): `skipMiddlewareUrlNormalize`->`skipProxyUrlNormalize`, `experimental.middlewarePrefetch`->`proxyPrefetch`, `experimental.externalMiddlewareRewritesResolve`->`externalProxyRewritesResolve`, types `NextMiddleware`->`NextProxy`, `MiddlewareConfig`->`ProxyConfig`, `MiddlewareMatcher`->`ProxyMatcher`, and `onRequestError` context `routeType` `'middleware'`->`'proxy'`.
Minimum supported versions raised: Node.js 20.9.0 (18.x no longer supported; engines field changed) and TypeScript 5.1.0.
The `next/legacy/image` component is deprecated with a warning; use `next/image`.
The `next lint` command is removed, `next build` no longer runs ESLint, and the `eslint` key in next.config is no longer supported; run ESLint or Biome directly.
The `NextConfig` type no longer extends `Record<string, any>`, so unknown or misspelled keys in a typed `next.config.ts` are now TypeScript errors.
Parallel route slots with routable children now require an explicit `default.js`; the build fails instead of silently 404ing at runtime.

`revalidateTag(tag)` now requires a second `cacheLife` profile argument (e.g. `'max'`) for stale-while-revalidate; the single-argument form is deprecated and is a TypeScript error, with `updateTag(tag)` for immediate expiry.
`serverRuntimeConfig` and `publicRuntimeConfig` (and `getConfig()` from `next/config`) are removed; use environment variables (`NEXT_PUBLIC_` for client values).
sass-loader is bumped to v16, which uses the modern Sass JS API; legacy-API `sassOptions` and the silenced legacy deprecation no longer apply.
The router no longer temporarily resets a global `scroll-behavior: smooth` during navigations; add `data-scroll-behavior="smooth"` on `<html>` to get the old override back.
The temporary synchronous access to `cookies()`, `headers()`, `draftMode()` and to the `params`/`searchParams` props kept for 15 is removed; these are Promises and must be awaited.
When a Babel config file is present, Turbopack now enables Babel automatically instead of exiting with a hard error.

Turbopack config keys moved: `experimental.turbopackPersistentCaching` is replaced by `experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForDev`/`ForBuild`, and `turbopack.moduleIds` becomes `experimental.turbopackModuleIds`.
`next dev`, `next build` and custom servers now use Turbopack by default instead of webpack; `--turbopack` is unnecessary, `--webpack` opts out, and a build with a `webpack` config and no flag fails.
`unstable_cacheLife` and `unstable_cacheTag` from `next/cache` are stabilized as `cacheLife` and `cacheTag` (the old names are still accepted but are no longer the documented imports).
`unstable_rootParams` is removed; use the `next/root-params` module.
The `experimental.clientSegmentCache` config key is removed; the segment cache router cannot be turned off any more.
`next build` now fails for App Router paths that normalize to the same route (e.g. `[slug]` vs `[modalSlug]` siblings) instead of letting the conflict surface at runtime.
Turbopack filesystem caching for `next dev` (`experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForDev`) is now on by default, persisting compiler artifacts under `.next` between runs.

In a `'use cache'` module, re-exports and exports of non-literal values (e.g. `export { getData } from`, `export const x = fn`) are now wrapped as cache functions at runtime, where previously only directly declared functions were.
The image optimizer's on-disk cache is now an LRU bounded by the new `images.maximumDiskCacheSize` (default: 50% of available disk space) instead of growing without limit.

Server Action CSRF validation now treats `Origin: null` (sandboxed iframes and other opaque contexts) as an explicit cross-origin value and rejects it unless `'null'` is listed in `experimental.serverActions.allowedOrigins`; it was previously treated as a missing origin and allowed.
`experimental.adapterPath` (Build Adapters) is promoted to the top-level `adapterPath` config key; the experimental location is deprecated.

`experimental.browserDebugInfoInTerminal` is replaced by `logging.browserToTerminal` (`boolean | 'error' | 'warn'`); the object form with `depthLimit`/`edgeLimit`/`showSourceLocation` is gone and the old key warns.
In development, browser `console.error`/`console.warn` output is now forwarded to the terminal by default (level `'warn'`) instead of only when opted in.
The dev server now blocks cross-origin requests to internal assets from origins not listed in `allowedDevOrigins`, where it previously only warned.
The image optimizer now rejects source images whose response body exceeds the new `images.maximumResponseBody` (default 50 MB), where previously any size was accepted.
`javascript:` URLs are rejected by `router.push`/`replace`, `redirect()` and related Next.js navigation APIs, which previously passed them through.
An outer `'use cache'` that nests a short-lived cache now must declare an explicit `cacheLife`; previously the default profile was silently used.
Importing React's taint APIs (`experimental_taintObjectReference` etc.) without `experimental.taint: true` is now a compile error instead of failing at runtime.
Turbopack now infers module side effects by default (`experimental.turbopackInferModuleSideEffects`), so imports it determines to be side-effect free can be dropped from bundles.
The tsconfig settings Next.js writes and checks no longer rely on `baseUrl` or `moduleResolution: "node"` (deprecated in TypeScript 6); `paths` now resolve without `baseUrl`.

Undocumented methods on the custom-server `next()` instance (`setAssetPrefix()`, `revalidate()`, logging helpers and the legacy `render*` helpers) are deprecated with warnings; use `getRequestHandler()`.
The Edge runtime (`export const runtime = 'edge'`) and the `preferredRegion` route segment config are deprecated with build warnings and `@deprecated` types; the Node.js runtime is the path forward.
Removed config keys: `experimental.turbopackMemoryLimit` and `experimental.viewTransition` (view transitions work without a flag).

The reworked App Router scroll and focus handling (`experimental.appNewScrollHandler`) is on by default: after navigation the active element is blurred instead of focusing the first focusable element in the segment.
The `opengraph-image` (and sibling image route) default export's return type is narrowed to `Response`; the other return types the types previously allowed failed the build.
`experimental.optimisticRouting` (client-side route prediction) is on by default, changing when navigations commit and which segments are fetched.
Requests to unknown paths whose `Sec-Fetch-Dest` is not a document (images, workers, manifest icons) now get a plain-text 404 instead of rendering the HTML not-found page.
`experimental.prefetchInlining` is on by default: small segment prefetches are bundled into one response per link instead of one request per segment.
Turbopack filesystem caching for `next build` (`experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForBuild`) is now on by default, so repeat builds reuse artifacts from `.next/cache`.
`experimental.turbopackTreeShaking` is renamed to `experimental.turbopackModuleFragments`.
`next build` type-checks with the project's TypeScript CLI by default (`experimental.useTypeScriptCli`, opt out with `false`) instead of the compiler API.

`experimental.validateRSCRequestHeaders` is on by default: an RSC request whose headers do not match the client's cache-busting search parameter is no longer served as an RSC response (previously only validated when opted in).
Turbopack production builds now generate shorter CSS Module class names (development keeps the long readable names).
Pages Router support for React 18 is deprecated: `next dev`/`next build` warn when React 18 is installed, ahead of removal in 17.

Client-side-rendering bailouts (`useSearchParams` without Suspense, resumed-render and CSR bailouts) now use React's `ReactDOM.browser` mechanism by default instead of throwing the Next.js bailout errors.

`experimental.strictRouteMatching` is on by default: App Router URLs that cannot build a complete route tree are rejected, unreachable pages and incompatible parallel-route slots are reported, and interception routes need a canonical route; `deprecated.looseRouteMatching: true` is the escape hatch.
Turbopack production builds now mangle internal export names by default (`experimental.turbopackMangleExportNames`), shortening the names used to connect modules.
Turbopack now emits its runtime as one chunk shared across routes (`experimental.turbopackSharedRuntime` on by default) instead of a per-route runtime.
Unrecognized Server Action IDs now return 400 (malformed) or 409 (unknown in this deployment) for both fetch and MPA form submissions, instead of 404 or 500.
`useReportWebVitals` moves to web-vitals v6: the FID metric is no longer reported and CLS/INP/LCP are now also reported for soft navigations with a `navigationURL`.

ResponseFunctionToolCallOutputItem.output (and ResponseCustomToolCallOutput.output) is typed string | Array<ResponseInputText | ResponseInputImage | ResponseInputFile> instead of string, so code that treats a function call output item's output as a plain string no longer type-checks
The Assistants API surface (client.beta.assistants create/retrieve/update/list/delete and the Assistant type) is marked @deprecated; it carried no deprecation before
The ComputerTool type now describes the GA computer tool (type 'computer'); the computer_use_preview tool it described before is renamed to ComputerUsePreviewTool
ResponseInputMessageItem.type ('message') is required instead of optional, so object literals of that type that omit it no longer type-check
The package's openai bin (the `openai migrate` codemod CLI from the v5 migration) is removed, so `npx openai migrate` no longer exists
The emitted(event) promise on the SDK's event streams and runners (ChatCompletionStream, runTools runners, AssistantStream) now rejects when an 'error' event fires instead of staying pending
Minimum supported Node.js rises from 20 to 22 (package.json engines >=22.0.0 added, Node version policy codified); Node 20 is no longer supported
embeddings.create called with encoding_format 'base64' now resolves to a response whose data[].embedding is typed string instead of number[] (a new overload); runtime behavior is unchanged
Rendering ARIA 1.3 attributes no longer triggers the DEV unknown-ARIA-attribute warning that it did before
A context is now named 'SomeContext' in component stacks, DevTools and warnings instead of 'SomeContext.Provider'
If a server-rendered (dehydrated) Suspense boundary resuspends on the client, React now hides its content and shows the fallback again instead of leaving the stale content visible
Streaming SSR now batches the reveal of server-rendered Suspense boundaries for a short time (matching client rendering) instead of swapping each fallback for its content the moment it arrives
When revealing server-rendered content React DOM now waits for pending (suspensey) fonts to load before the reveal instead of revealing immediately
useId generates IDs in the form _r_... (underscore delimiters) instead of «r» (19.1) / :r: (19.0), so they are valid CSS selectors, XML names and view-transition-names
Using a React-owned DOM node that also contains text content as a root container now logs a DEV warning where it was silent before
State updates triggered by resize events are batched until the next frame instead of being processed per event
DEV now warns when a component appears to have been unblocked by calling use() conditionally, which was silent before
The list of CSS shorthand properties behind the DEV shorthand/longhand style-conflict warning was updated, changing which style combinations warn
When React automatically resets a form after its action completes, the form's onReset handler now fires; previously the automatic reset did not fire it
The FormData handed to a form action is now built with the submitter, so the submitting button's name/value is included as in the native FormData constructor; before it was left out
credentialless on <iframe> is now a recognized boolean attribute (true renders the bare attribute, false omits it) instead of being rendered as a stringified unknown attribute
React.lazy now treats the resolved module's .default export as the canonical component type for identity comparisons instead of the lazy wrapper's own resolution
Rendering data-block <script> elements (non-executable types such as application/json) no longer triggers a DEV warning
defaultValue on <input type=number> is now synced to the DOM the same way as on other input types instead of the number-specific handling used before
The DEV DOM-nesting validation for <select> follows the new HTML <select> parser rules, changing which children are allowed inside <select> without a warning
During server-rendering error recovery a tree that never completed is now treated as an error instead of being accepted as finished
react-dom/server streaming APIs no longer call onAllReady after the shell has errored, where previously it could still fire
In StrictMode effects are now double-invoked during hydration too, matching client-rendered roots, where hydrated roots were previously exempt
StrictMode's DEV double-invocation no longer re-runs effects for children that only moved (were reordered) rather than remounted
Concurrent transitions render independently instead of being entangled into one render, so a slow transition no longer delays unrelated ones
React DOM passes Trusted Types objects (TrustedHTML/TrustedScript/TrustedScriptURL) through to DOM sinks instead of coercing them to strings, so they now work under a require-trusted-types-for CSP
moduleResolution bundler may now be combined with module commonjs; before, that combination was rejected with a program error and bundler required module esnext or preserve.
tsc given file arguments in a directory that has a tsconfig.json now fails with TS5112 instead of silently ignoring the config; the new --ignoreConfig flag restores the old behavior.
allowSyntheticDefaultImports now defaults to true and setting it to false is a deprecation error, so default imports from modules without a default export are always allowed for type-checking.
alwaysStrict false is deprecated; all code is parsed as strict mode, so sloppy-mode identifiers such as await, static, private or public are now syntax errors.
The /// <amd-module name="..." /> directive is deprecated together with module amd and no longer has any effect.
baseUrl is deprecated and is no longer a lookup root for bare module specifiers; paths entries must carry the prefix themselves (a "*" catch-all mapping restores the old lookup).
Setting downlevelIteration at all, even to false, is now a deprecation error where 5.9 accepted it silently; it only ever affected the now-deprecated es5 emit.
esModuleInterop now defaults to true and setting it to false is a deprecation error, so CommonJS modules are always imported with interop semantics (import x from "m" rather than import * as x).
Import assertions are deprecated: import x from "./a.json" asserts { type: "json" } and import("./a.json", { assert: {...} }) are errors; use the with keyword and the with option instead.
The module values amd, umd, system and none are deprecated and error unless ignoreDeprecations is "6.0"; ESM or commonjs emit with a bundler replaces them.
Declaring a namespace with the module keyword (module Foo {}) is a deprecation error; write namespace Foo {} (ambient declare module "x" {} is unaffected).
moduleResolution classic is deprecated (an error unless ignoreDeprecations is "6.0"); nodenext or bundler replaces it.
moduleResolution node (node10) is deprecated in favor of nodenext or bundler; setting it is an error unless ignoreDeprecations is "6.0".
The /// <reference no-default-lib="true"/> directive is deprecated and no longer supported; use noLib or libReplacement instead.
outFile is deprecated (an error unless ignoreDeprecations is "6.0"); concatenated single-file output needs an external bundler.
target es5 is deprecated (an error unless ignoreDeprecations is "6.0"); es2015 is the lowest supported target and ES5 output needs an external compiler.

lib dom now contains everything from dom.iterable and dom.asynciterable, so iterating a NodeList or HTMLCollection works with lib: ["dom"] alone; dom.iterable and dom.asynciterable are now empty files.

Under exactOptionalPropertyTypes, property comparison no longer treats a missing optional property as equivalent to undefined, so { p?: string } and { p?: string | undefined } are no longer identical types.

Generic calls and generic JSX elements that take function expressions are checked more strictly (the any-function wildcard is a subtype but no longer a supertype of function types, and JSX children propagate non-inferrable flags), so some calls now report implicit any or need an explicit type argument.
libReplacement defaults to false instead of true, so @typescript/lib-* packages in node_modules no longer replace the built-in lib files unless the option is set explicitly.
An unset module now means esnext; before it meant commonjs under the old es5 default target (es2015 for newer targets).

The computed moduleResolution default for module es2015 through esnext is bundler instead of classic (so the new esnext default resolves as bundler); commonjs keeps node10 and the deprecated module values keep classic.
noUncheckedSideEffectImports defaults to true instead of false, so a side-effect import of a module that cannot be resolved is an error by default.
An unset rootDir now means the directory containing tsconfig.json instead of the inferred common directory of the input files, so src/index.ts emits to dist/src/index.js unless rootDir is set.
The strict option defaults to true instead of false, so a project with no strict setting now gets every strict check (noImplicitAny, strictNullChecks and the rest).
An unset target now means the latest standard ECMAScript version (es2025 in 6.0, a floating default) instead of es5, so modern syntax is no longer downleveled by default.

A function or method that never uses this is no longer treated as context-sensitive during generic inference, so method-syntax callbacks with untyped parameters now infer from sibling properties regardless of property order instead of falling to unknown.

An unset types now means [] instead of every package under node_modules/@types, so globals from @types/node, @types/jest and similar are only visible when listed in types (types: ["*"] restores the old behavior).

Calls in .js files use TypeScript's arity rules: with strict false, arguments for parameters typed undefined, unknown or any can no longer be omitted, and using arguments inside a function body no longer implies a ...args: any[] parameter.

In CommonJS JavaScript files, nested undeclared exports (exports.N.X.p = 1), an ignored empty module.exports = {}, this as an alias of module.exports, var x = require("m").prop, aliasing module.exports to a variable and mixing module.exports = ... with module.exports.x = ... are no longer supported, and repeated exports.x assignments union instead of narrowing.
Declaration (.d.ts) emit from .js input files is rewritten and no longer matches 6.0's output, especially when the input has errors; supported JSDoc tags keep their semantics.

In JavaScript files, constructor functions (this.x inside a function plus prototype assignments), fallback initializers (f.x = f.x || v), nested undeclared expandos (N.X.Y = {}), typed this.x; declarations without an initializer, this aliases (var that = this) and top-level this as globalThis are no longer treated as declarations; use classes and explicit assignments.

JSDoc in .js files follows TypeScript rules: a variadic {...T} is only an array synonym and no longer makes a parameter a rest parameter, {T=} no longer adds undefined when strictNullChecks is off, an asserts return annotation on an arrow must go on the variable's @type, @typedef and @callback in a class body hoist out of it, a @param applies to at most one function, @type assertions block narrowing, and @overload is ignored on arrow and function expressions.

In JavaScript files, Closure-era JSDoc forms are no longer recognized: a standalone ? type, module:path namepath types, @class/@constructor, @enum, identifier-named typedefs (/** @typedef {T} */ Name;), function(string): void function types, postfix ! and bare values used as types (write typeof v).

The typescript package no longer exports the compiler API: lib/typescript.js and typescript.d.ts are gone and import ts from "typescript" only yields the version; tools must alias typescript to @typescript/typescript6 until a new API ships in 7.1.
The package's engines field requires Node.js >=16.20.0, up from >=14.17 in 5.9 and 6.0.
allowSyntheticDefaultImports can no longer be set to false at all (hard error, no ignoreDeprecations escape).
alwaysStrict is always true and setting it to false is a hard error; sloppy-mode code is no longer accepted.
The /// <amd-module /> directive, deprecated in 6.0, is removed together with module amd.
baseUrl, deprecated in 6.0, is removed and is a hard error; paths entries must be written relative to the project root.
downlevelIteration, deprecated in 6.0, is removed; setting it is a hard error.
esModuleInterop can no longer be set to false at all (hard error, no ignoreDeprecations escape); interop import semantics are always on.
The asserts keyword on imports (and assert in import() options), deprecated in 6.0, is a hard error; only with is accepted.
The module values amd, umd, system and none, deprecated in 6.0, are removed and are hard errors; esnext or preserve with a bundler replaces them.
module Foo {} namespace syntax, deprecated in 6.0, is a hard error; only namespace Foo {} is accepted.
moduleResolution classic, deprecated in 6.0, is removed and is a hard error.
moduleResolution node (node10), deprecated in 6.0, is removed and is a hard error; nodenext or bundler replaces it.
/// <reference no-default-lib /> directives, deprecated in 6.0, are no longer respected at all, including under skipDefaultLibCheck.
outFile, deprecated in 6.0, is removed and is a hard error.
target es5, deprecated in 6.0, is removed: it is a hard error that ignoreDeprecations no longer silences, and es2015 is the lowest target.
Conflicting declarations are reported at every contributing declaration instead of sometimes only one, so conflicts that skipLibCheck previously hid entirely now surface in non-.d.ts files.

Types and symbols are ordered by a deterministic content-based algorithm (6.0's stableTypeOrdering flag) and this cannot be turned off, so union member order in declaration emit and hovers, and occasionally inference results, differ from 6.0's default ordering by type ID.

Inference through template literal types consumes whole Unicode code points instead of UTF-16 code units, so `${infer H}${infer T}` on a string starting with an emoji yields the emoji and the rest rather than two surrogate halves; type-level string utilities that counted code units break.
The tsserver executable and lib/tsserver.js are no longer shipped (bin holds only tsc); editors integrate through the new Language Server Protocol server instead.
A plain-object value given to .default()/.prefault() is cloned on each parse instead of the same object instance being returned every time.

.extend() on an object schema that carries refinements throws instead of silently dropping the refinements (narrowed in 4.3.1 to throw only when an existing key is overwritten; .safeExtend() is the supported path).
z.uuid() accepts the all-F 'Max UUID' (FFFFFFFF-FFFF-FFFF-FFFF-FFFFFFFFFFFF) that it previously rejected.
The inferred output type of z.promise(T) is Promise<output<T>> instead of the unwrapped output<T> (z.promise() was already deprecated).
z.e164() requires a non-zero leading digit and 7-15 digits in total, rejecting some phone strings it accepted before.

The mask given to .pick()/.omit()/.partial()/.required() (and the Zod Mini functions) is a TypeScript error when it names a key not in the shape; such keys previously type-checked, though the runtime already threw.
.pick() and .omit() on an object schema that carries refinements throw instead of silently dropping the refinements.
A type-predicate function passed to .refine() narrows the schema's output type; previously the predicate was ignored and the output type was unchanged.
Registering a schema under an id already in a registry overwrites silently instead of throwing; duplicate ids are instead rejected by z.toJSONSchema().
An intersection that includes z.strictObject() rejects only keys unrecognized by both sides; previously a key unknown to either side failed the parse.
Zod Mini schemas no longer expose a .refine() method; use .check(z.refine(fn)) instead.
z.cuid(), the .cuid() chain method and the related CUID v1 classes and regex export are marked @deprecated in favor of z.cuid2().

z.toJSONSchema() output changes in four places: no redundant id inside $defs entries, different min/max for intersections under the draft-04 and openapi-3.0 targets, a recursive z.lazy() with .describe() converts instead of overflowing the stack, and falsy prefault values (0, '', false) are emitted as default where they were omitted.
.merge() throws when the receiving object schema has refinements instead of producing ambiguous refinement behavior; refinements on the argument schema are kept.

Three string formats are stricter: z.base64() rejects whitespace it used to tolerate, z.cuid() accepts only c plus at least 6 base36 characters (its JSON Schema pattern follows) instead of any 8 or more non-space, non-hyphen characters, and z.httpUrl() rejects a single slash after the scheme (https:/example.com) that the URL constructor used to repair.

Tuple parsing writes element defaults into the output (filling positions before a defaulted element with undefined); previously defaults in tuple positions were not materialized, and tuple-length errors, including z.function() argument errors, changed shape.
Object properties typed z.undefined(), z.any() or z.unknown() require the key to be present at parse time (the value may be undefined); Zod 4.0-4.3 accepted a missing key.

ZodError output for unions changes: z.treeifyError() and z.formatError() keep the full path of issues nested inside unions, and invalid-discriminator issues from z.discriminatedUnion() carry the discriminator options and a reworded message.
z.discriminatedUnion() option schemas must have the discriminator key in their input type; options that lack it are now TypeScript errors.
z.iso.datetime() (with or without offset: true) rejects minute-precision input such as 2020-01-01T06:15Z that it accepted before; local: true still allows it.

z.toJSONSchema() behaves differently for inputs it already handled: a root schema with an id in its metadata is emitted as a root $ref into $defs, a union of simple primitive types becomes a type array instead of anyOf, and the override callback runs before the unrepresentable error is thrown.

ZodNumberFormat takes a format type parameter so ZodInt, ZodFloat32, ZodFloat64, ZodInt32 and ZodUInt32 (and the bigint formats) are distinct at the type level instead of one interchangeable type (commit marked with !).
Object and record parsers always drop a __proto__ key (from input, schema or key transform), and .strict() reports an own __proto__ input key as unrecognized_keys instead of swallowing it.
A record's key schema governs only keys that match it, so intersecting an object with a pattern-keyed record no longer rejects the object's own keys as invalid_key.
The ZodError produced by .safeParse() no longer captures a stack trace at construction, so result.error.stack is not the call site it used to be.

Several string formats are stricter: z.ipv6() checks the address alphabet directly instead of via new URL() (rejecting ::1 followed by a newline), z.ulid() requires a first character of 0-7, z.httpUrl() enforces the RFC 1035 host length limits, the z.emoji() regex no longer backtracks exponentially, and the JSON Schema pattern for .includes(sub, { position: N }) allows at least N leading characters instead of exactly N.
String .min()/.max()/.length() count Unicode code points instead of UTF-16 code units, so astral characters such as emoji count once.
An unrecognized_keys issue no longer aborts the object it came from, so a strict object with an extra key and a bad value reports both issues instead of the first alone.

The runtime regexes behind z.base64()/z.base64url() check only the alphabet with length and padding enforced in code (z.regexes.base64url becomes the length-aware form), and the z.email() pattern (z.regexes.email, issue.pattern and the JSON Schema pattern) drops its lookaheads and capture groups; composing either into a template literal no longer applies the dropped rules to the rest of the string.
z.emoji() rejects strings made only of emoji components (digits, #, *, lone modifiers or joiners) such as "123" that it previously accepted.
.safeParse() builds its ZodError lazily, so error maps (global, locale and per-schema error) run when result.error is first read rather than at parse time.
z.toJSONSchema() folds chained checks as a conjunction, so a later format check no longer overwrites tighter min/max bounds and repeated multipleOf or min/length chains emit the correct constraints.

Schema members .format, .minLength, .maxLength, .minValue, .maxValue, .isInt, .minDate and .maxDate are prototype getters materialized on first read (absent from Object.keys until then) and report the tightest bound rather than the last-written one.
z.enum(NumericEnum).options lists only the numeric values; the reverse-mapping member names that it used to include (and that failed to parse) are gone.
